plain_text:
Like a camera, your eyes rely on a lens—the clear part of
the eye that helps focus light on the retina. A cataract
is a clouding of that lens, which can affect your vision.
Most cataracts develop from aging. By age 80, more than half of
Americans either have a cataract or have had cataract surgery.
semantic_text: Like a camera, your eyes rely on a lens—the clear part of the eye that helps focus light on the retina. A cataract is a clouding of that lens, which can affect your vision. Most cataracts develop from aging. By age 80, more than half of Americans either have a cataract or have had cataract surgery.

plain_text:
You may be at a higher risk if you smoke, consume alcohol
excessively, or have a family history of cataracts. Spending a lot
of time in the sun without sunglasses can also raise your chances
of cataracts. Diabetes and steroid use can also cause cataracts.

plain_text:
The National Eye Institute (NEI) has helpful resources on the
condition, its symptoms, and treatment options.
semantic_text: The National Eye Institute (NEI) has helpful resources on the condition, its symptoms, and treatment options.

plain_text:
■ Cloudy or blurry vision
■ Changes to how colors look (they may seem faded)
■ Seeing a glare (headlights, lamps, or sunlight may appear too
bright or you might see a halo around lights)
■ Poor night vision
■ Double vision or seeing multiple images in one eye
(this symptom may clear as the cataract gets larger)
■ Frequent prescription changes to your eyeglasses or
contact lenses

plain_text:
These symptoms aren't always specific to cataracts—they can
also signal other eye problems. If you have any of these symptoms,
be sure to check with your eye care professional.

plain_text: Although most cataracts are related to aging, there are other types:
semantic_text: Although most cataracts are related to aging, there are other types:

plain_text:
■ Secondary cataracts can form after surgery for other eye
problems (such as glaucoma).
■ Traumatic cataracts can develop after an eye injury,
sometimes even years later.
■ Pediatric cataracts are present at birth or develop in
childhood, often in both eyes. These cataracts may be so
small that they do not affect vision. If they do, the lenses
may need to be replaced.
■ Radiation cataracts can develop after exposure to some
types of radiation.
semantic_text: ■ Secondary cataracts can form after surgery for other eye problems (such as glaucoma). ■ Traumatic cataracts can develop after an eye injury, sometimes even years later. ■ Pediatric cataracts are present at birth or develop in childhood, often in both eyes. These cataracts may be so small that they do not affect vision. If they do, the lenses may need to be replaced. ■ Radiation cataracts can develop after exposure to some types of radiation.

plain_text:
The symptoms of an early cataract may improve with new
eyeglasses, brighter lighting, antiglare sunglasses, or magnifying
lenses. If these measures do not help, surgery is the only effective
treatment. Surgery involves removing the cloudy lens and replacing
it with an artificial lens.
semantic_text: The symptoms of an early cataract may improve with new eyeglasses, brighter lighting, antiglare sunglasses, or magnifying lenses. If these measures do not help, surgery is the only effective treatment. Surgery involves removing the cloudy lens and replacing it with an artificial lens.

plain_text:
There are some things you can do to lower your chances
of cataracts. They include:
semantic_text: There are some things you can do to lower your chances of cataracts. They include:

plain_text:
■ Wearing sunglasses and a hat with a brim to protect your
eyes from the sun
■ Wearing protective eyewear while doing activities such
as using power tools or playing certain sports
■ Quitting smoking (or don't start!)
■ Eating fruits, leafy green vegetables, fish, nuts, whole grains,
and other foods rich in vitamins that are good for eye health
